{"id":"PKIX-rm8.29","title":"pkix-path-builder::Error::NoValidPath carries last_error as String, not typed","description":"pkix_path_builder::Error::NoValidPath { tried: usize, last_error: String } carries the last validation error as a Display-rendered String rather than a typed pkix_path::Error. The variant doc explains this is because pkix_path::Error does not implement Hash (which Error derives). However this means callers who need to programmatically distinguish failure reasons (e.g. 'the only candidate chain had an expired intermediate' vs 'the only candidate chain had an unrecognized signature algorithm') must parse a free-form Display string or iterate build_path_candidates themselves.

The error is carried as String specifically to preserve Hash on the Error enum. pkix_path::Error does not impl Hash because it contains DerError (which uses Box<str>). The tradeoff was deliberate, but the contract consequence is that NoValidPath is the only Error variant in the entire workspace that discards typed error information for a derive convenience.

What goes wrong if this stays as-is: Callers who receive NoValidPath cannot programmatically distinguish between different validation failures without dropping to the raw iterator API. The pkix-chain crate works around this (lines 618-631 in pkix-chain/src/lib.rs) by catching NoValidPath and re-running build_path (topology-only, no validation) to get a chain and re-validate it — specifically so the caller gets a typed pkix_path::Error rather than the stringified version. This workaround proves the typed error is needed by at least one consumer.

{"notes":"Analysis 2026-11-25: the stated obstacle is now REMOVED. The remaining change is purely a semver decision.

Both beads (they are duplicates of each other -- see below) correctly identify the justification: NoValidPath stores last_error as a Display-rendered String so pkix_path_builder::Error keeps its Hash derive, because pkix_path::Error does not implement Hash.

Traced that to its root rather than accepting it. pkix_path::Error failed to derive Hash because of EXACTLY ONE variant: Der(DerError). DerError is first-party (pkix-path/src/lib.rs:180), holding { inner: Option<der::Error>, message: BoxStr }, and its PartialEq is already hand-written comparing `message` alone.

So Hash was four lines, and its correctness is guaranteed by that existing PartialEq: Hash requires equal values to hash equally, equality here is defined solely by message, so hashing solely message cannot violate it. Done in this commit, together with #[derive(Hash)] on pkix_path::Error. Both are additive and non-breaking.

It had to be hand-written, not derived: a derive would include `inner`, which serde drops on deserialize (it cannot be rebuilt from the rendered message) while equality IS preserved -- so a derive yields two equal values with different hashes. Test error_der_hash_agrees_with_eq_across_the_round_trip pins this, and fails if inner is hashed.

What remains: changing NoValidPath { last_error: String } to hold a typed pkix_path::Error. That is now possible with no obstacle, but it changes a public struct-variant field type, which is breaking even though the enum is #[non_exhaustive] (non_exhaustive protects against added VARIANTS, not retyped FIELDS). So it belongs with the other queued breaking changes: PKIX-lnnl.4, PKIX-rm8.27, PKIX-rm8.44, and the q9hv.19/q9hv.29 pair.

Duplicate note: PKIX-rm8.29 and PKIX-wnnn.5 are the same finding about the same field, citing the same rustdoc justification. Neither is empty -- each adds detail the other lacks. rm8.29 names the escape hatch (iterate build_path_candidates yourself). wnnn.5 adds two further costs: serde round-trip cannot preserve the inner variant structure, and a caller cannot retry on specific failure modes. Keeping both pointed at each other rather than superseding one, so no analysis is lost; whoever does the work should read both."}

Fixed, per your ruling to cut one breaking release. Error::NoValidPath.last_error is now a pkix_path::Error, not a String.

Both beads were right, and they are duplicates of each other -- closing both with the same record so neither reads as superseded-and-empty.

The obstacle was removed first: pkix_path::Error failed to derive Hash because of exactly one variant, Der(DerError), and DerError is first-party with a hand-written PartialEq comparing only its message field. So Hash was four lines, provably consistent with that PartialEq, and had to be hand-written because a derive would include the inner der::Error that serde drops on deserialize while equality is preserved. Commit 000ac209.

Two consequences beyond the field, both worth more than it:

1. std::error::Error::source() now returns the inner failure. The impl was empty before because a String has no cause to return. Error chains work from here.

2. pkix-chain stopped rebuilding chains. This closes PKIX-rm8.45 as a side effect: the driver used to drop NoValidPath payload with `{ .. }`, re-run topology-only build_path, and hand the result back for the caller to re-validate -- purely to recover a structured error. That could report a DIFFERENT chain failure, since build_first_valid_path prunes candidates by signature and build_path does not. PoolVerdict::OnlyUnvalidated now carries the builder own error, both use sites report it, and assemble_unvalidated is deleted.

Detail each bead contributed, now both addressed: rm8.29 named the escape hatch (iterate build_path_candidates yourself) -- no longer needed. wnnn.5 added that serde round-trip could not preserve the inner variant structure and that a caller could not retry on specific failure modes -- both now possible, and pkix-path-builder serde feature enables pkix-path/serde so the field actually round-trips.

Test improvement worth noting: a test asserted only !last_error.is_empty(), which ANY message satisfies. It now asserts the variant -- AlwaysRejectVerifier must surface as SignatureInvalid rather than an expiry or name mismatch. That assertion was impossible with a String.

Gates green: fmt, clippy, rustdoc, 2357 tests, workspace feature powerset 241 combinations clean.
